Description: Coil spring (circular wire, mean radius 10, wire radius 2, so the wire occupies the radial band 8..12) and a coaxial cylinder of radius 7. The two solids are completely disjoint - the cylinder fits into the free bore of the coil without touching it.
Expected: union: two separate solids, total volume 2368.705 + 3694.513 = 6063.218. intersect: empty (E_NOT_FOUND or an empty result). difference both ways: the respective operand unchanged.
Status: union FIXED (re-checked 2026-08-10): returns two separate solids as expected. intersect STILL WRONG - this file is now the canonical case for that.
Actual: solid.boolean intersect returns 2368.6613, i.e. operand a (the coil), although the two bodies are disjoint and the intersection must be empty. The same symptom shows up whenever the operands merely touch instead of overlapping: thread + rod r=5, coil + cylinder r=8 (tangent) and rectCoil + cylinder r=10 (coincident face) all return exactly V(a) as the intersection. It looks like the 'no intersection found' branch returns the target unchanged instead of an empty result.
Actual (before the fix): union returned a single solid with the volume of the coil, i.e. the cylinder was silently dropped; intersect returned the coil as well. Only the two differences were correct.
